questions.:question/problem:
Given that
$$
C=\begin{bmatrix}4 & 6 & 2 \\ 3 & 6 & 4 \\ 2 & 3 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{22}=0?$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{3}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =\begin{bmatrix}4 & 6 & 2 \\ 3 & 6 & 4 \\ 2 & 3 & 1\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}4 & 6 & 2 \\ -1 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 1\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{3}.
$$

questions.:question/problem:
Given that

$$
C=\begin{bmatrix}3 & -10 & 6 \\ -1 & -8 & -4 \\ -9 & 0 & 7\end{bmatrix}
$$

which of the following elementary row operations makes $a_{22}=0$?
questions.:question/worked-solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation

$$
{R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}.
$$

The entry in row $3$, column $2$ is $0$. Switching rows $2$ and $3$ therefore makes $a_{22}=0$.

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}C &=\begin{bmatrix}3 & -10 & 6 \\ -1 & -8 & -4 \\ -9 & 0 & 7\end{bmatrix}\qquad {R}_{2}↔{R}_{3} \\ &\sim \begin{bmatrix}3 & -10 & 6 \\ -9 & 0 & 7 \\ -1 & -8 & -4\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}.
$$

canonical_example.:question/problem:
Given that

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 5 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{bmatrix}
$$

 which elementary row operation could make $a_{22}=0?$
canonical_example.:question/worked-solution:
In the given matrix, we have $a_{22}=5$ and we want to perform an elementary row operation that makes $a_{22}=0.$

- We *cannot* make $a_{22}=0$ by switching two rows, because there are no rows with $0$ as the second entry.

- We *cannot* multiply the second row by $0,$ because we are only allowed to multiply rows by *nonzero* constants.

- However, we *can* add a multiple of another row to the $2$nd row to make $a_{22}=0.$

Looking at the first row, we see that $a_{12}=1.$ If we add $-5$ times this entry to $a_{22},$ we will get $a_{22}=0$ as desired. So, the elementary row operation that we need to use is

$$
R_2 := R_2 + (-5) \cdot R_1.
$$

Applying this operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 5 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{bmatrix}\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-5)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1+(-5)\cdot 3 & 5+(-5)\cdot 1 & 6+(-5)\cdot (-2) \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{bmatrix} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -16 & 0 & 16 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the desired elemetary row operation is

$$
R_2 := R_2 + (-5) \cdot R_1,
$$

or simply

$$
R_2 := R_2 -5 R_1.
$$
